chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: Falling ill in Dallas with pleurisy and nearly dying
summary: Cobb takes sick on a trip to Dallas, is brought home at 119 pounds, and is found to have pleurisy; a doctor treats him at home and in Jefferson Davis Hospital.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: ... pieces. And we went up to Dallas, and I took sick up there. And I was a guy that believed in taking my money and putting it in a sock, and putting a safety pin in it, and when I put the safety pin in it, that means one thing. Don't spend it. But I neglected myself, and took sick. I didn't eat properly.
I see. Yeah. You were trying to save too much.
I don't know ... it was in '34.
I'm gonna let you all figure it, because I ain't that good in mathematics. I took 18½ months of accounting, but when you pinpoint me, I have to get a pencil and paper.

'34. And, he had to get permission -- I was young enough for him to get permission from my mother to take me away, and somebody said they saw me on crutches up there, and that was twice -- and Chester loved those crutches, and everybody thought we were brothers. But not knowing that I was sick, too; I was in the bed and Chester got me out of the bed to come to the phone to talk to my mother, because her boyfriend said, 'I'll pay for this call'. And he put the coins in, and she asked me, 'Baby, how you doing?' And I'd say 'Fine.' Sick as a dog! And Stanley, I wouldn't lie to you. But he told me to say it, and I was a youngster, so what did I know?

He brought me in to Houston; I was weighing 172 pounds, and when I came back to Houston, I weighed 119½, and you could count every rib on my body. And when he come in that driveway and brought my mother from where she was working,
that was where he brought me. You know, I had pleurisy, and didn't even know it.

Yes sir. I was getting ready to tell you something now. My mother felt like she wanted to kill him. She wanted to go and get her boss's gun and kill him. But I guess the presence of it pressed on her mind and she didn't do it. And when she carried me to the doctor, and they had what you call -- she was a tuberculosis specialist, but I had pleurisy. Dr. Robie. I don't know if she's dead or alive today. But that woman was something else.

But she told my mother and she examined me, and told her it was just a matter of time -- too late. That's medical science for you. I was 15. I can tell you how old I was then. I was 15 years old -- or 16. Somewhere in there, 15 or 16. And here I am, that young, gonna die with pleurisy?

And she put me in Jefferson Davis Hospital here, but first she come to my house, hit me with them big needles, about half as big as my little finger, and shoot that dope in me, or whatever it was, and I could feel them pushing on me, you know. But they were pumping fluid up there, and she came to my house first. You don't have anybody come to your house today -- you know that, don't you?
But she came to my house and did it. Had a pan and shoot that fluid out to me, and then after she got it to a certain level, she brought me to the hospital. And I ain't
dead yet! I'm 59 years old today. Medical science said I was dead.
